marks.gloss_en: אזכרתן מילתא דאמר רבי יהושע בן לוי -- purchase from a gentile exempts from terumat maaser, so R' Chanina's 'it is his' is terumat maaser (an amoraic dictum adduced; no SupportKind names one)
one who buys smoothed tevel from a gentile is exempt from terumat maaser
if the gentile smoothed it, it would owe no tithe at all: 'your grain' and not a gentile's grain (a verse-refutation; no ObjectionKind names one)
(entertained) R' Chanina speaks of produce the gentile himself smoothed

טעמא דמספקא לן אי חלפינהו אי לא חלפינהו, הא ודאי חלפינהו -- דכולי עלמא בעי למיתבינהו לכהן; והאמר רבי שמואל אמר רבי חנינא: הלוקח טבלים מן הגוי ממורחין -- מעשרן והן שלו! (amoraic-memra contradiction; kind svara under protest)
דלמא כאן בתרומה גדולה, כאן בתרומת מעשר -- the mishna's giving-to-the-kohen is teruma gedola; R' Chanina's 'it is his' is terumat maaser (= p_kan_tg_kan_tm)
perhaps here [the mishna, must give] is teruma gedola, there [R' Chanina, his] is terumat maaser
one who buys smoothed tevel from a gentile tithes it, and it is his
rather, an Israelite smoothed it while it was in the gentile's domain
one who deposits his produce with a Kuti or an am haaretz -- it keeps its presumptive status for tithe and for shevi'it
with a gentile -- it is like his [the gentile's] produce
as to separating [teruma and tithes], all agree [he must]
and if [the lamb of a firstborn donkey's redemption] died, one may derive benefit from it
(hava amina) as long as it has not reached his hand, [the kohen] has not acquired it
